exact_items: cross-family historical terms: historical, stale_historical, superseded, revoked, reopened, archived, removed
historical: queryable past object/state that is no longer the currently active focus
stale_historical: historical and explicitly not resumable/reusable for live execution
superseded: replaced by a newer canonical successor in the same lineage
revoked: previously accepted/promoted/active decision or state explicitly withdrawn
reopened: previously closed/accepted path returned to active question or work
archived: intentionally retained but removed from default active presentation
removed: live backing removed while historical identity may still persist
do not force family-local workflows into the cross-family semantic core

resolved as single interpretation across all families
notes: consistency here means shared meaning, not one single lifecycle enum for every object family

seed_items.canon_label_hint: Projection trust model with 5 operational states: current/refreshing/stale/degraded/unavailable; mutation controls gated on trusted projections; fallback to record-backed views when degraded
exact_items: Define one shared projection-trust contract with operational state meanings and action thresholds:
- `current`: projection is up to date enough for normal read + write interaction
- `refreshing`: slightly behind but actively catching up; read is fine, write may still be fine
- `stale`: data is old enough that mutation-bearing actions should narrow or require refetch
- `degraded`: projector or dependency failure means surface may be incomplete or partially wrong
- `unavailable`: projection cannot currently support that surface; UI must fall back or disable
Require all dense Orchestrator tabs to show freshness/last-updated/disclosure state.
Gate mutation controls on trusted projections or explicit runtime revalidation.
Standardize fallback toward record-backed views (History, Ledger, exact record inspectors) when projections are degraded.
stale_tokens: if data is visible, it is safe to act on it
notes: stale visibility is not the same as action authority
blocked/recovery controls are especially sensitive because allowed_action_ids[] can go invalid if projection trust drops
